RagShortTexts: The 13th-century coat of plates riveted shaped iron plates inside leather to counter heavy.

Variants.Content: Faced with crushing warhammers and heavy crossbow bolts, traditional mail hauberks proved inadequate. Armourers developed the coat of plates: overlapping iron plates riveted within a stout canvas or leather surcoat. This hybrid defence absorbed concussion while preserving torso mobility, paving the path toward full plate harness.

Armourers in Milan and Nuremberg now craft tailor-fitted plates beneath rich velveteen shells. Gilded rivets trace heraldic motifs across the chest, combining chivalric prestige with vital protection against direct missile strikes.

A mace strike through plain mail shatters ribs without cutting the skin. But with shaped iron plates riveted over your chest, a spear point skates right off. That leather-and-iron vest makes all the difference in a breach.
